frontMatter.introduction:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual establishes a structured framework for the operational processes followed at Quality Rubbers. It is designed to ensure consistency, efficiency, and control across all business activities, including procurement, processing, quality management, storage, and dispatch.

The SOP defines standardized procedures, responsibilities, and controls required for effective execution of operations and compliance with applicable regulatory and customer requirements. It serves as a reference document to guide employees in performing their roles in a systematic and consistent manner.

The implementation of this SOP supports effective process management, product quality, workplace safety, and overall operational performance within the organization.
frontMatter.objective:
The objectives of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) are to:
Establish standardized procedures for all key operational activities to ensure consistency and efficiency.
Define roles, responsibilities, and controls required for effective execution of processes.
Ensure compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, and customer requirements.
Maintain product quality through controlled processing, handling, and storage practices.
Promote safe working conditions and responsible operational practices.
Improve resource utilization and minimize operational inefficiencies.
Support effective monitoring, documentation, and record-keeping across all functions.
Facilitate continuous improvement in operational performance and overall business practices.
frontMatter.scope:
This policy applies to all employees, workers, directors, officers, contractors, and any third parties acting on behalf of Quality Rubbers. It covers all business activities associated with the Company's operations, including sourcing of raw rubber materials, cleaning and upgrading processes, storage, handling, transportation, and dispatch of materials, as well as interactions with customers, suppliers, regulatory authorities, and other stakeholders.

The Human Resource Management system at Quality Rubbers establishes structured processes and guidelines for workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, and employee management to ensure compliance with applicable laws and organizational requirements.

blocks.text: To ensure recruitment is conducted in a structured, fair, and legally compliant manner, with appropriate controls to verify identity, eligibility, and compliance with minimum age requirements.

steps.heading: Advertising approved vacancies

body.text: Approved vacancies are advertised through appropriate internal and external channels to attract a diverse and qualified candidate pool.

steps.heading: Screening applications

body.text: Applications are screened based on objective, job-related criteria, including qualifications, experience, and role-specific competencies.

steps.heading: Anonymizing resumes

body.text: Where feasible, resumes may be anonymized during initial screening to minimize the risk of unconscious bias and promote fair evaluation.

steps.heading: Conducting structured interviews

body.text: Structured interviews are conducted by Human Resources and relevant departmental representatives to assess technical skills, experience, and overall suitability for the role.

steps.heading: Making selection decisions

body.text: Selection decisions are based on a consolidated assessment of candidate performance, evaluation scores, and panel feedback to ensure objectivity.

steps.heading: Informing candidates of outcome

body.text: Candidates are informed of the outcome of their application in a timely manner, and feedback may be provided where appropriate.

steps.heading: Verifying identity and date of birth

body.text: As part of the recruitment and onboarding process, verification of identity and date of birth is conducted to ensure compliance with applicable legal requirements, including minimum working age. Candidates are required to submit valid government-issued identity documents (such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Birth Certificate, or School Leaving Certificate), which are verified prior to finalization of employment.

blocks.text: All recruitment activities are carried out in accordance with applicable legal, ethical, and labour standards, ensuring equal opportunity and non-discriminatory practices throughout the process.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and representatives of Quality Rubbers who engage in transactions that may carry a real or perceived personal benefit alongside a business benefit. Such transactions are inherently higher risk for corruption and must be subject to prior written approval.
Sensitive transactions are discretionary transactions where there is, or could be perceived to be, a personal benefit in addition to a business benefit. They commonly arise in the following contexts:

Hospitality — meals, entertainment, sporting events, or cultural events offered to or received from clients, suppliers, government officials, or other external stakeholders.
Business gifts — physical gifts, gift cards, vouchers, or tokens of appreciation given or received in a professional capacity.
Travel — business travel arrangements that include personal extensions, upgrades, or companion travel at company or client expense.
Sponsorships and charitable donations — contributions that could be perceived as a means to obtain a business advantage.
Facilitation payments — any payment made to expedite a routine government action, regardless of amount.
The following thresholds apply. All values are per transaction and per recipient/donor within a 12-month rolling period:

rows: Line Manager — verbal approval; log in team register
Line Manager — written approval via email; log in compliance register
Line Manager + Compliance Officer — written approval required before transaction
Senior Management + Compliance Officer + MD — formal approval memo required
Compliance Officer sign-off mandatory regardless of value

steps.heading: Employee identifies a potential sensitive transaction

body.text: Employee identifies a potential sensitive transaction (giving or receiving).

steps.heading: Employee completes the Sensitive Transaction Request Form

body.text: Employee completes the Sensitive Transaction Request Form (Form QR-ETH-01) detailing: nature of transaction, estimated value, business justification, parties involved, and timing.

steps.heading: Form is submitted to Line Manager for initial review

body.text: Form is submitted to Line Manager for initial review.

steps.heading: Line Manager reviews for business necessity and proportionality

body.text: Line Manager reviews for business necessity and proportionality. If approved, escalates to Compliance Officer if thresholds require.

steps.heading: Compliance Officer reviews against Anti-Bribery Policy

body.text: Compliance Officer reviews against Anti-Bribery Policy, applicable laws, and counterparty restrictions (e.g., government/public sector rules).

steps.heading: Decision is recorded in the Compliance Register

body.text: Decision (approval or rejection) is recorded in the Compliance Register within 2 business days.

steps.heading: Employee is notified and may proceed only upon written confirmation

body.text: Employee is notified and may proceed only upon written confirmation of approval.

steps.heading: Post-transaction: Employee submits receipt/invoice and final value

body.text: Post-transaction: Employee submits receipt/invoice and final value within 5 business days for record-keeping.

sops.title: Protection of Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access

blocks.text: This procedure governs the access, storage, handling, and disposal of all customer, client, supplier, and employee data held by Quality Rubbers. It applies to all digital and physical data assets across all departments and locations.
All third-party data held by Quality Rubbers must be classified as follows before any access or handling:

rows: Personal financial data, contract pricing, health records, government IDs, passwords
Business contact details, procurement terms, internal reports, HR records
General operational data, non-sensitive internal communications
Marketing materials, published product catalogues, public financial disclosures

blocks.text:
All systems containing third-party data must implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Access is granted on a strict need-to-know basis only.
Unique user credentials are mandatory. Shared logins are strictly prohibited.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) must be enabled for all systems accessing Highly Confidential or Confidential data.
All data in transit must be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. All data at rest must be encrypted using AES-256 or equivalent.
Remote access to company systems must use an approved VPN. No data may be accessed via unsecured public networks without VPN.
All system access events (login, data export, failed login attempts) must be automatically logged and retained for a minimum of 12 months.

Physical documents containing Confidential or Highly Confidential data must be stored in locked filing cabinets with key access restricted to authorized personnel.
Printed sensitive documents must not be left unattended on desks or shared areas.
Secure document disposal — all physical documents containing personal or confidential data must be shredded using a cross-cut shredder. Standard waste bins must not be used.
Visitor access to areas where sensitive data is processed must be controlled and logged.

A full access audit of all data systems must be conducted annually by the IT/Compliance team. Results must be reported to senior management.
Access rights must be reviewed and revoked immediately upon employee departure or role change.
Any suspected unauthorized access, data breach, or loss of data must be reported to the Data Protection Officer (DPO) within 24 hours of discovery.
The DPO will initiate the Data Breach Response Protocol (QR-DPO-02), which includes root-cause analysis, stakeholder notification, regulatory reporting (if applicable), and remediation.

rows: Implement and maintain technical access controls, encryption, and audit logs
Policy oversight, breach response, regulatory compliance
Handle data per classification; report any breach immediately
Ensure access revocation upon staff departure
Annual access audit and policy review

blocks.text: This procedure applies to all waste generated from office operations and production activities at Quality Rubbers facilities. It establishes the operational framework for waste identification, segregation, collection, and recycling to minimize landfill disposal.

steps.heading: WASTE STREAM IDENTIFICATION

body.text: Before recycling can be operationalized, all major waste streams must be identified and quantified. Department heads are responsible for conducting a waste audit within their areas of responsibility every 12 months. Waste streams to be catalogued include:

Paper and cardboard (office and packaging)
Plastics (packaging films, bottles, containers — segregated by resin code where feasible)
Metals and aluminum (cans, scrap from operations)
Glass (bottles, laboratory glassware)
Electronic waste / e-waste (computers, cables, batteries, toner cartridges)
Rubber off-cuts and production scrap (specific to manufacturing operations)
Organic / food waste (from canteen and kitchen areas)

steps.heading: Waste generated at source

body.text: Waste generated at source (desk, workstation, production line) must be deposited into the correctly labelled bin for that waste stream.

steps.heading: Facilities staff collect and consolidate waste

body.text: Facilities staff collect and consolidate segregated waste from all areas daily and transfer to the designated waste holding area.

steps.heading: Waste holding area

body.text: Waste holding area must be clearly marked, covered, and separate from general storage. Access is restricted to authorized personnel.

steps.heading: Certified recycling vendor collection

body.text: Certified recycling vendor collects recyclable materials on a scheduled basis (minimum weekly). Vendor must hold valid environmental permits.

steps.heading: Waste transfer documentation

body.text: Waste transfer documentation (consignment notes/manifests) must be signed and retained for a minimum of 3 years.

steps.heading: Waste quantities recorded monthly

body.text: Waste quantities (by stream) must be recorded monthly in the Waste Management Register (QR-WM-01).

steps.heading: Annual recycling rate

body.text: Annual recycling rate (% of total waste recycled vs. disposed to landfill) must be calculated and reported to management.

rows: Deposit waste in correct labelled bins at point of generation
Manage waste holding area, vendor liaison, maintain waste register
Annual waste audit within their area; target ownership
Report waste metrics to management; drive improvement
Ensure recycling vendor holds valid permits; contract renewal

blocks.text: To systematically reduce paper consumption across all Quality Rubbers operations through policy, technology, and behavioral change — reducing both environmental impact and operational cost.

steps.heading: Default duplex printing

body.text: Default duplex (double-sided) printing must be enabled on all networked printers and copiers. Single-sided printing requires manual override and should be used only when strictly necessary (e.g., legal originals, client-facing documents).

steps.heading: Digital distribution and approval

body.text: All internal reports, memos, approvals, and meeting materials must be distributed and approved digitally. Printing for internal circulation is not permitted unless requested by a Head of Department in writing.

steps.heading: Electronic signatures

body.text: Electronic signatures (via approved platforms) must be used for all internal document approvals and contracts wherever legally permissible.

steps.heading: Annual form review

body.text: All forms currently issued in paper format must be reviewed annually by the respective department. Forms that can be completed digitally must transition to digital within 6 months of identification.

steps.heading: Primary document storage

body.text: Shared network drives and document management systems must be the primary location for all document storage. Personal local drives and physical files must not be used as primary storage.

narrative.text:
Secure print release (PIN or swipe card at printer) must be implemented on all office printers to reduce uncollected print jobs.
Monthly paper consumption data (reams purchased/used per department) must be tracked and reported by the Facilities team.
Departments exceeding their paper budget must provide a written justification to the Sustainability Officer.

blocks.text:
Paper-saving tips to be included in new employee onboarding.
Quarterly reminders to be issued via internal communications (email, notice boards, intranet).
To ensure all operational waste is correctly segregated at source into defined waste streams prior to disposal, enabling compliant treatment, recycling, and recovery of materials.

steps.heading: WASTE SEGREGATION INFRASTRUCTURE

body.text: The following bin/container infrastructure must be maintained at all Quality Rubbers locations:

steps.heading: Waste bins must be placed at all points of significant waste generation

body.text: Waste bins must be placed at all points of significant waste generation — each workstation, kitchen area, print station, reception, and production floor section.

steps.heading: All bins must be clearly and permanently labelled

body.text: All bins must be clearly and permanently labelled with the waste category name, accepted items, and items NOT accepted. Visual symbols (icons) should supplement text labelling.

steps.heading: Employees are responsible for placing waste in the correct bin

body.text: Employees are responsible for placing waste in the correct bin. If unsure, employees must consult the Waste Sorting Guide posted in each area or contact the Facilities team.

steps.heading: Bins must not be allowed to overflow

body.text: Bins must not be allowed to overflow. Facilities staff must empty bins at a frequency that prevents overflow — no less than once per working day for high-use areas.

steps.heading: Hazardous waste (red bins) must be collected by a licensed hazardous waste contractor

body.text: Hazardous waste (red bins) must be collected by a licensed hazardous waste contractor and must not be mixed with general or recyclable waste under any circumstances.

steps.heading: Contaminated recyclables must be placed in the general waste stream

body.text: Contaminated recyclables (e.g. food-soiled paper) must be placed in the general waste stream, not the recycling stream.

steps.heading: Waste sorting compliance audits must be conducted quarterly

body.text: Waste sorting compliance audits must be conducted quarterly by the Facilities Manager. Non-compliance must be reported and corrective action taken within 5 business days.

blocks.text: Incorrect waste sorting undermines recycling rates and may result in regulatory penalties. Persistent non-compliance by employees will be addressed through the company performance management process.

sops.title: Energy Efficiency Through Technology and Equipment Upgrades

blocks.text: To reduce the company's total energy consumption and operational costs by systematically replacing energy-intensive equipment and processes with more efficient alternatives.

steps.heading: Annual energy audit

body.text: A comprehensive energy audit of all facilities must be conducted annually by a qualified energy auditor (internal or external).

steps.heading: Identify significant energy-consuming assets

body.text: The audit must identify all significant energy-consuming assets (SECAs) — typically assets consuming more than 5% of total facility energy.

steps.heading: Establish baseline energy consumption

body.text: Baseline energy consumption data (kWh per unit of output and per employee) must be established and maintained in the Energy Register (QR-EN-01).

steps.heading: Annual benchmarking against industry peers

body.text: Benchmarking against industry peers must be conducted annually to identify areas where the company's energy intensity is above sector average.

steps.heading: Identify upgrade candidates

body.text: Identify upgrade candidates from the annual energy audit. Prioritize assets with high energy intensity, age above useful life, or below 4-star energy rating.

steps.heading: Prepare Technology Upgrade Proposal

body.text: Engineering/Facilities team prepares a Technology Upgrade Proposal (Form QR-EN-02) for each candidate, including: current consumption data, proposed replacement specification, expected energy savings, capital cost, and payback period.

steps.heading: Approval of proposals

body.text: Proposals with a payback period of 5 years or less are automatically approved for budget submission. Longer payback periods require MD sign-off with sustainability justification.

steps.heading: Procurement of approved upgrades

body.text: Approved upgrades are scheduled and procured via the standard procurement process, with energy efficiency as a mandatory evaluation criterion (minimum weighted score: 25%).

steps.heading: Post-installation measurement

body.text: Post-installation energy consumption is measured and compared to baseline for 6 months. Results are documented and shared with senior management.

blocks.text:
Lighting: LED lighting across the facility. Motion-sensor controls in low-occupancy areas (storerooms, corridors, restrooms).
HVAC: Replace units below ISEER 3.5 with inverter-based systems. Install programmable thermostats with occupancy scheduling.
Compressed Air Systems: Fix all air leaks identified in quarterly leak surveys. Upgrade to variable-speed drive (VSD) compressors.
Production Machinery: Procure only IE3 / IE4 rated electric motors for all new and replacement installations.
IT Equipment: Enforce power management settings on all computers. Replace desktops with energy-efficient laptops where operationally feasible.

sops.title: Reduction of Emissions from Transportation and Fleet

blocks.text: To reduce Scope 1 and Scope 3 GHG emissions associated with company-owned fleet operations, employee commuting, and logistics transportation.

steps.heading: All company vehicles must be registered in the Fleet Management System

body.text: All company vehicles must be registered in the Fleet Management System (FMS) with fuel type, mileage, and emission factor recorded.

steps.heading: Route optimization software must be used for all scheduled deliveries and collections

body.text: Route optimization software must be used for all scheduled deliveries and collections. Routes must be reviewed monthly to identify consolidation opportunities.

steps.heading: Driver behavior monitoring (telematics) must be active on all vehicles

body.text: Driver behavior monitoring (telematics) must be active on all vehicles. Harsh braking, excessive idling (>3 minutes), and speeding events must be reviewed with drivers monthly.

steps.heading: Vehicle maintenance schedules must be strictly observed

body.text: Vehicle maintenance schedules must be strictly observed. Out-of-service vehicles must not be used. Tyre pressures must be checked weekly — under-inflated tyres increase fuel consumption by up to 3%.

blocks.text: Car-sharing and carpooling scheme must be actively promoted. A dedicated car-sharing platform (app or noticeboard) must be maintained at each facility.
Video/teleconference must be the default for all internal meetings. Travel to in-person meetings requires manager approval if a VC option is available.
Rail must be the preferred mode for all domestic business travel under 500 km. Air travel for short-haul journeys must be justified in writing.
A public transport subsidy or electric vehicle charging allowance may be offered to employees as part of the Green Commute Incentive Program.
To build company-wide awareness, knowledge, and behavioral change around energy conservation and climate action, making every employee an active participant in the company's GHG reduction goals.

Monthly Green Tips to be distributed via email and posted on the intranet and physical notice boards.
Annual 'Energy Challenge' — inter-departmental competition to reduce energy consumption over a 4-week period.
Earth Hour (last Saturday of March) and World Environment Day (5 June) to be marked with company-wide awareness activities.

An internal environmental impact review shall be performed across all key stages of operations.
The lifecycle stages shall include raw material procurement, transportation, cleaning, processing, grading, storage, and dispatch activities.
Environmental aspects including resource consumption, energy usage, material loss, and waste generation shall be monitored at each stage.
Findings from the review shall be used to identify opportunities for environmental improvement and process optimization.

sops.title: Regular Assessment of Individual Employee Performance

blocks.text: To establish a structured, fair, and consistent process for evaluating employee performance that supports individual development, organizational alignment, and recognition of top contributors.
Each annual appraisal must evaluate the employee against the following dimensions, with a rating of 1 (Below Expectations) to 5 (Exceptional):

Goal Achievement — assessment against goals set at the previous appraisal or onboarding.
Technical Competency — proficiency in the skills, knowledge, and tools required for the role.
Behavioral Competencies — alignment with Quality Rubbers values (Integrity, Innovation, Sustainability, Collaboration, Customer Focus).
Sustainability Contribution — specific contribution to the company's sustainability, safety, or ethical objectives.
Professional Development — progress against personal development goals and training completed.

sops.title: Employee Health and Safety Risk Assessment

blocks.text: To systematically identify, evaluate, and control hazards that could cause harm to employees, contractors, visitors, or other affected parties at Quality Rubbers facilities and across its supply chain operations.

steps.heading: RISK ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK

body.text: All risk assessments must address all three of the following elements:

Hazard Identification: A systematic description of all hazards and risk factors present in the workplace or operational context with the potential to cause harm. Hazards must be categorized as: Physical, Chemical, Biological, Ergonomic, Psychosocial, Environmental, Supply Chain/ESG, Information Security, or Governance/Compliance.
Periodic Review of Risks: The risk register must be formally reviewed at least annually, and immediately following any workplace incident, near-miss, significant process change, or new regulatory requirement.
Preventive and Corrective Action Plan: A documented set of control measures (eliminate, substitute, engineer, administrate, PPE — in order of hierarchy) and remediation steps for each identified risk.

steps.heading: Health & Safety Officer (HSO) schedules annual risk assessment for each facility area and work function.

body.text: Health & Safety Officer (HSO) schedules annual risk assessment for each facility area and work function.

steps.heading: Assessment team (HSO + department representative + employee representative) conducts physical walkthrough and hazard identification.

steps.heading: Each hazard is assessed for Probability of Occurrence (1–5) × Impact Level (1–5) = Risk Rating (1–25). Risk ratings are categorized as: Low (1–8), Medium (9–16), High (17–25).

sops.title: Actions to Promote Equal Opportunity for All Employees

blocks.text: To foster a diverse, equitable, and inclusive (DEI) workplace at Quality Rubbers where every employee has an equal opportunity to contribute, grow, and succeed, free from discrimination of any kind.

Quality Rubbers strictly prohibits discrimination, harassment, or unfair treatment on the basis of: gender, gender identity, age, race, ethnicity, caste, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy, national origin, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. This applies to recruitment, promotion, training, compensation, and all other employment decisions.

Employee Resource Groups (ERGs): Quality Rubbers supports formally recognized ERGs (e.g., Women in Manufacturing, Young Professionals Network, Differently-Abled Allies). ERGs must have a senior sponsor and access to a modest annual budget.
Mentoring Programme: A structured mentoring scheme pairing senior and junior employees across different functions and backgrounds. Participation is voluntary but actively encouraged. Minimum 6-month pairing duration.
Leadership Pipeline: At least 30% of internal promotion candidates at managerial level and above must be from underrepresented groups (defined annually by the DEI Committee).
Accessibility: All facilities to be assessed for accessibility compliance annually. Reasonable adjustments must be made for employees with disabilities within 30 days of request.
Inclusive Recruitment: All job postings must use inclusive language (reviewed by HR). Interview panels must include at least one gender-diverse member. Structured interview scoring matrices must be used.

narrative.text:
Annual DEI Report (internal) to be prepared by HR and submitted to the Board, covering: workforce diversity data, pay equity analysis, inclusion survey results, and progress against DEI targets.
All employees must complete annual unconscious bias and inclusion training.
A confidential grievance mechanism (hotline or online portal) must be available for reporting discrimination or harassment. All reports must be investigated within 15 business days.

blocks.text: To ensure that all suppliers providing goods and services to Quality Rubbers are assessed against defined sustainability criteria, and that supply chain risks related to environmental harm, labor violations, and governance failures are identified and managed.

steps.heading: Supplier Segmentation

body.text: Not all suppliers carry the same level of sustainability risk. Suppliers must be segmented annually as follows to ensure proportionate assessment:

rows: High spend, direct material suppliers, suppliers in sensitive geographies or industries
Indirect material suppliers, services suppliers, moderate spend

steps.heading: Sustainability Assessment Criteria

body.text: The Supplier Sustainability Assessment (Form QR-PR-01) must cover the following domains:

Environmental Management: Does the supplier have an environmental policy? Do they track and report energy, water, and waste data? Do they hold ISO 14001 or equivalent?
Labor Standards: Are wages at or above legal minimum? Are working hours compliant with local law? Is there a zero-tolerance policy for child and forced labor? Are there safe working conditions?
Health & Safety: Does the supplier have an H&S management system? What is their recordable incident rate?
Business Ethics & Governance: Does the supplier have an anti-bribery policy? Is there a grievance mechanism for workers? Have there been any regulatory violations in the past 3 years?
Product Sustainability: Does the supplier use certified or sustainable materials? Do they have a product take-back or circular economy program?

steps.heading: Identify and segment active suppliers

body.text: Procurement team identifies all active suppliers and segments them by risk tier annually (by 31 January each year).

steps.heading: Issue assessment forms

body.text: Assessment forms are issued to suppliers by 28 February. Suppliers have 30 days to complete and return.

steps.heading: Review assessments and assign scores

body.text: Procurement team reviews completed assessments and assigns a Sustainability Score (0–100) to each supplier.

steps.heading: Categorise scores

body.text: Scores are categorized: Preferred (80–100), Acceptable (60–79), Requires Improvement (40–59), At Risk (<40).

steps.heading: Manage at-risk suppliers

body.text: Suppliers scoring 'At Risk' must be placed on a formal Supplier Improvement Plan with a 6-month review. Failure to improve results in removal from the approved supplier list.

steps.heading: Schedule on-site audits

body.text: On-site audits (for Tier 1 suppliers) must be scheduled and conducted with at least 48 hours notice (unannounced for high-risk cases).

steps.heading: Store and share results

body.text: Assessment results must be stored in the Supplier Register and shared with the Sustainability Committee quarterly.

blocks.text: To ensure that Quality Rubbers's supplier selection and procurement processes are free from discrimination and provide equal opportunity to all eligible suppliers regardless of size, geography, ownership, or background.

Non-discrimination: Supplier selection must be based solely on objective performance criteria (quality, price, delivery, sustainability). No supplier may be excluded or disadvantaged on the basis of ownership demographics, size, geographic location, or association with any protected group.
Equal access: All procurement opportunities above INR 100,000 must be advertised through at least two channels (e.g., company website, industry portal, direct outreach) to ensure broad market access.
Local sourcing preference: Where two or more suppliers are otherwise equivalent in quality and price, the supplier providing greater local economic benefit (employment, local materials, community investment) will be preferred. This preference shall not override significant quality or compliance differentials.
SME and diverse supplier development: Quality Rubbers will set an annual target for the percentage of procurement spend with SMEs and diverse-owned businesses (women-owned, minority-owned, disability-owned).

All tender evaluation panels must include at least 3 members from different functions. No single individual may make a final supplier selection decision above INR 500,000.
Conflict of interest declarations must be completed by all panel members before each evaluation.
Unsuccessful suppliers have the right to request a written debrief on the reasons for their non-selection. Debriefs must be provided within 10 business days of request.
Procurement team must complete annual training on inclusive sourcing practices and unconscious bias in supplier evaluation.
